title: Tools
summary: Every pickaxe, axe, hoe, scythe and fishing rod with its tier, stats, ability and how to make it.

s.x: Tools are how you gather. SkyRPG has a ladder of pickaxes, axes, hoes and scythes, and fishing rods, each made at the
from the one before it. Tools carry gathering stats (Mining Speed, Fortune, Fishing Speed...) that apply while you hold them, and the better ones have a right-click ability. Tools
as you use them, but a SkyRPG tool never disappears: at 1 durability it is broken until you repair it (see Durability and repair below).
A pickaxe's Mining Speed and Mining Fortune only count while it is in your hand. Gathering stats from armour, talents and enchants add on top.
Pickaxes and axes have a tier from I to VII. SkyRPG's harder ores and woods need a minimum tier, and a weaker tool does not crack them at all (see
The better tools have a right-click ability with a cooldown. They do not cost mana.
The bench keeps a tool's name and enchantments when you upgrade it.
Pickaxes, axes, hoes (scythes count as hoes), any tool and fishing rods each take their own kind of enchant (see
Every pickaxe, axe, hoe, scythe and fishing rod has a durability that grows with its tier, so the tools you use most last longest. Weapons, armour, shields, bows, wands, backpacks and accessories do

rows.x: Quarry Pick, Woodsman Axe, Harvester Hoe

s.x: For comparison, vanilla's wooden tools have 59, iron 250, diamond 1,561 and netherite 2,031. The tooltip and the bar under the item show what is left.
A pickaxe or axe loses 1 durability for each block it breaks. A hoe or scythe loses 1 for each ripe crop you harvest (and when it tills soil). A rod loses 1 each time you reel in.
, the scythes' 3x3 and 5x5 sweeps and the extra ore of a Veinseeker or Hellfire Vein cost only 1 durability per 4 extra blocks, so felling a whole tree costs a few points, not thirty.
Creative mode never wears a tool.
A SkyRPG tool never breaks for good. When it would, it stays at

and the action bar says "Your tool is broken, repair it". A broken tool mines at hand speed, drops nothing that needs a tool, counts as no tier, gives none of its stats, perks or enchants, cannot use its ability and cannot till, strip or cast, until it is repaired. Treefeller and sweeps stop when the tool runs out.
Anvil with the tool's own material.

Put the tool and its material in an anvil; each piece restores a quarter of its durability, as in vanilla. Iron-tier tools (Quarry Pick, Delver's Pickaxe, Woodsman Axe, Ironbark Hatchet, Harvester Hoe, Thornfield Sickle, Sunreaper Scythe) take
, diamond-tier tools (Prospector, Skyiron, Duskbore and Emberheart Pickaxes, Mistpine Splitter, Willowcleaver, Frostbite and Cinder Scythes) take
, and netherite-tier tools (Hellforged Pickaxe, Lumen Breaker, Emberbrand Axe, Starwood Greataxe, Moonlit Reaper) take
. Two of the same tool also combine into one in an anvil. Your SkyRPG enchants stay on the tool.

Hold the damaged tool and right-click Brannoc: he quotes a price for mending it completely, and a second right-click pays it. Sneak and right-click to open his shop as usual. The price is per missing durability point: 0.4 coins for Common, 0.6 Uncommon, 0.8 Rare, 1 Epic and 1.2 for Legendary tools (a completely worn-out Lumen Breaker costs about 4,800 coins).

s.x: Every pickaxe ability has its own look and sound: Echo Sense sweeps sonar rings out across the stone and each ore flares (with a chime that is higher the closer it is) as the wave reaches it, Skyward Burst fires streaks of wind upward, Molten Core and Hellfire Vein flare with embers and flame, and Lumen Pulse bathes you in white-blue light. Scythes and the Moonlit Reaper have their own gusts of leaves, snow or moonlight. The item shows its recharge as a dark sweep over its slot.
